title: Crisp Garden Salad with Honey-Mustard Vinaigrette
summary: A crunchy, colourful garden salad finished with a honey-mustard vinaigrette that balances sharp cider vinegar against a touch of honey.
equipment: salad spinner or clean tea towels
small bowl or jam jar with a lid

ingredients.item: green leaf or butterhead lettuce (1 head)
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Wash and dry leaves
steps.text: Wash the lettuce thoroughly in plenty of cold water, then dry it very well in a salad spinner, working in batches, or roll it in a clean tea towel. Tear into bite-size pieces by hand and keep chilled until you're ready to serve. Any water left clinging to the leaves dilutes the vinaigrette and stops it clinging properly.

steps.title: Whisk the vinaigrette
steps.text: In a small bowl or jam jar, whisk together the cider vinegar, mustard powder, honey, salt, pepper and 1 tsp water. Whisking steadily (or shaking hard in the jar for about 20 seconds), add the olive oil in a thin stream until the mixture thickens slightly. The mustard powder acts as an emulsifier, helping the oil and vinegar bind instead of separating.

steps.title: Dress the vegetables
steps.text: In the large salad bowl, toss the halved cherry tomatoes, sliced cucumber, radishes and red onion with 2 tbsp of the vinaigrette. Dressing these firmer vegetables first lets them pick up flavour evenly without crushing the delicate lettuce underneath.

steps.title: Add leaves and toss
steps.text: Just before serving, add the chilled lettuce to the bowl and drizzle over the rest of the vinaigrette a little at a time. Toss gently by hand until the leaves are lightly glossed, not drenched — adding the dressing gradually stops them wilting under too much liquid. Serve at once.

tips: Dry the lettuce thoroughly; wet leaves stop the dressing from clinging and leave it pooling at the bottom of the bowl.
Dress the lettuce only at the last minute so it stays crisp rather than wilting.
Whisk the oil in slowly for a vinaigrette that stays combined rather than splitting.
Shake the vinaigrette again before using if it has been sitting, as it can separate slightly.
storage: Keep the undressed lettuce and vegetables separately, covered, in the fridge for up to 2 days. Once dressed the salad wilts quickly, so toss only what you'll eat and finish it the same day; the vinaigrette alone keeps in a sealed jar in the fridge for about a week. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
